jung-advanced-transcendent.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche
jung-advanced-transcendent.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-transcendent.reference: Collected Works 8, “The Transcendent Function,” §§131–193; written 1916, revised for publication 1958; primary chapter bibliographic record.

jung-advanced-types-symbol.title: Psychologische Typen
jung-advanced-types-symbol.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-types-symbol.reference: 1921 German edition, Chapter XI, definitions “Symbol” and “Transscendente Funktion”; compare CW 6, §§814–829.

jung-advanced-types-enantiodromia.title: Psychologische Typen
jung-advanced-types-enantiodromia.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-types-enantiodromia.reference: 1921 German edition, Chapter XI, definition 18, “Enantiodromie”; compare CW 6, §709. Historical interpretation, not a universal empirical law.

jung-advanced-inflation.title: Two Essays on Analytical Psychology
jung-advanced-inflation.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-inflation.reference: CW 7, “The Relations between the Ego and the Unconscious,” Part I, chapters II and IV(b), inflation and identification with the collective psyche; IAAP institutional chapter abstracts verify bibliography, not full text.

jung-advanced-types-constructive.title: Psychologische Typen
jung-advanced-types-constructive.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-types-constructive.reference: 1921 German edition, Chapter XI, definitions “Construktiv,” “Reduktiv,” and “Phantasie”; constructive and reductive methods.

jung-advanced-energy.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche
jung-advanced-energy.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-energy.reference: CW 8, “On Psychic Energy” (1928), Part I, the energic viewpoint and quantitative estimation; IAAP institutional abstracts verify primary work and chapter structure.

jung-advanced-energy-progression.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche
jung-advanced-energy-progression.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-energy-progression.reference: CW 8, “On Psychic Energy,” Part III(a), “Progression and regression”; distinction between progression and psychological development.

jung-advanced-energy-regression.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche
jung-advanced-energy-regression.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-energy-regression.reference: CW 8, “On Psychic Energy,” Part III(a), “Progression and regression”; activation of unconscious contents in regression.

jung-advanced-types-individuation.title: Psychologische Typen
jung-advanced-types-individuation.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-types-individuation.reference: 1921 German edition, Chapter XI, definition 31, “Individuation”; compare CW 6, §§757–762, social relationship and distinction from individualism.

jung-advanced-stages.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche
jung-advanced-stages.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-stages.reference: CW 8, “The Stages of Life” (1930–31), pp. 387–403 in the Princeton collected edition; historical model of life phases.

jung-advanced-religion.title: Psychology and Religion: West and East
jung-advanced-religion.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-religion.reference: CW 11, “Psychology and Religion,” Terry Lectures (1937), chapters 1–3: numinosum, experience and creed, psychological inquiry and metaphysical claims. Institutional chapter abstracts, not full text.

jung-advanced-anima.title: Two Essays on Analytical Psychology
jung-advanced-anima.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-anima.reference: CW 7, “The Relations between the Ego and the Unconscious,” Part II, chapter II, “Anima and animus”; historical binary/gender assumptions explicitly criticized in the card.

jung-advanced-types-soul.title: Psychologische Typen
jung-advanced-types-soul.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-types-soul.reference: 1921 German edition, Chapter XI, definitions “Seele” and “Seelenbild”; complementarity and historical sex-role generalizations.

jung-advanced-types-image.title: Psychologische Typen
jung-advanced-types-image.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-types-image.reference: 1921 German edition, Chapter XI, definition 8, “Bild”; the inner image and its psychological actuality distinguished from sensory reality.

jung-advanced-alchemy.title: Psychology and Alchemy
jung-advanced-alchemy.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-alchemy.reference: CW 12, Part III, “Religious Ideas in Alchemy,” chapter 2, “The psychic nature of the alchemical work,” and chapter 5, “The lapis–Christ parallel”; Jung’s historical/psychological interpretation, institutional chapter bibliography.

jung-advanced-mandala.title: The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious
jung-advanced-mandala.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-mandala.reference: CW 9i, “Concerning Mandala Symbolism,” pp. 355–384 and appendix “Mandalas,” pp. 385–390 in Princeton 1968 edition; ordering and context.

jung-advanced-wholeness.title: Psychology and Religion: West and East
jung-advanced-wholeness.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-wholeness.reference: CW 11, “Answer to Job,” discussion of completeness, moral perfection, and the relation of opposites; wholeness treated as a psychological problem, institutional chapter bibliography.

jung-advanced-synchronicity.title: The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche
jung-advanced-synchronicity.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-synchronicity.reference: CW 8, “Synchronicity: An Acausal Connecting Principle” (1952), exposition, experiment, and conclusion; theory distinguished from established evidence. Institutional primary-work abstracts.

jung-advanced-types-concretism.title: Psychologische Typen
jung-advanced-types-concretism.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-types-concretism.reference: 1921 German edition, Chapter XI, definition 11, “Concretismus”; fusion of thought/feeling with sensory object. Colonial classifications criticized in the card.

jung-advanced-amplification-primary.title: Psychology and Alchemy; The Symbolic Life
jung-advanced-amplification-primary.author: C. G. Jung
jung-advanced-amplification-primary.reference: CW 12, §403, amplification through association and analogy; CW 18, The Tavistock Lectures (1935), §§173–174, comparative interpretation. These passages and exact paragraph references are reproduced/discussed by the IAAP institutional article; this link is not the full primary edition.

jung-advanced-amplification-institutiona.title: Dreams
jung-advanced-amplification-institutiona.author: Yasuhiro Tanaka, International Association for Analytical Psychology
jung-advanced-amplification-institutiona.reference: Section “The dream is a spontaneous and natural occurrence”: amplification as seeking parallels, citing Jung CW 18, §§172–174; contextual and interpretive limits. Institutional scholarly explanation.

jung-advanced-amplification-example.title: Genesis
jung-advanced-amplification-example.author: Hebrew Bible; World English Bible translation
jung-advanced-amplification-example.reference: Genesis 28:10–17, Jacob’s dream of a ladder joining earth and heaven. The promotion example and psychological comparison are original illustrations of amplification, not Jung’s case material.
